title: Build and justify a normal form
prompt: In explicit row order (p,q)=FF,FT,TF,TT, a function has outputs F,T,T,F. Construct an equivalent DNF and CNF, then justify both on every valuation.
rubric: The DNF includes exactly the two true rows.
The CNF excludes exactly the two false rows.
Both formulas agree with F,T,T,F in the declared row order.
Equivalent reordered or redundant forms are not rejected solely for their spelling.
reference: A DNF is (¬p∧q)∨(p∧¬q). A CNF is (p∨q)∧(¬p∨¬q).
For FF both formulas are false; FT and TF make both true; TT makes both false. Equivalent formulas may have a different appearance.

title: Explain validity and satisfiability separately
prompt: For p→q, identify which condition is sufficient and which is necessary. Explain why premises p→q and p entail q. Then explain why premises p and ¬p entail q vacuously, and whether those second premises are jointly satisfiable.
rubric: In p→q, p is sufficient for q and q is necessary for p; the direction is not reversed.
Invalidity requires one valuation where all premises are true and the conclusion is false.
The first argument has no such valuation.
The inconsistent premise set has no jointly satisfying valuation, so it has no counterexample row.
Vacuous validity is kept distinct from the truth or satisfiability of the premises.
reference: In p→q, p is sufficient for q and q is necessary for p. For premises p→q and p, a true p forces q true when the implication premise is true. Thus no premise-true/conclusion-false row exists.
No valuation makes both p and ¬p true, so the second argument is valid vacuously; its premises are unsatisfiable. This does not make q a tautology.
